question: In drop-enabled generated rules, how many positions contain a quiet (non-checking) drop that the served quiescence policy excludes but that creates a new attack on an undefended enemy piece, and do those positions show a larger depth-2 vs depth-3 served score change than positions without such an excluded drop?
changed_premise: Prior DEEPSEEK_AUX work measured the hand-term coefficient (sensitivity, truncation, move classes) and material-transition semantics. None of it measured whether the documented conservative quiescence inclusion rule (ordinary quiet drops stay out) hides materially meaningful drops at the even-depth leaf. This asks a different question about a different code path with new seeds.

inputs.generator_seed_note: Fresh seed range; not used by the closed hand-term panel (59-94), the material-transition panel (7/11/13, 21-26) or the asymmetric-static panel (281001-281006).
inputs.start_position_recipe: deterministic Random(seed*1009+offset) walk, offset 0 first; take the first state at ply_count>=10 with >=6 legal actions and no terminal child; up to 4 offsets; record offset and ply.
inputs.search: run_root_search, use_tt=False, use_ordering=True, TranspositionTable(20000), SearchLimits(max_depth=d, max_nodes=20000, quiescence_max_depth=4, quiescence_hard_max_depth=8)

measurement.excluded_drop: legal drop action that classify_noisy does not return for the position (ordinary quiet drop; terminal and checking drops are included by policy and counted separately as controls)
measurement.blind_threat: after applying an excluded drop, the mover's pseudo_attacks contain a square occupied by an enemy piece that was not attacked before the drop and that is not attacked by any enemy piece after the drop (is_square_attacked by the enemy). Value uses profile.board_value_by_type of the attacked piece and of the dropped base type.
measurement.confirmation: for each blind-threat drop, one depth-1 search from the child position with the same limits; record child_score (negated to the mover's perspective) and whether it exceeds the parent's static-free baseline

decision_rule_written_before_run.support: >=3 of 12 positions contain at least one blind-threat drop AND the blind-threat group's median abs(score_d3-score_d2) is at least 2x the median of the remaining positions (or the group's action-flip rate is at least 2x and the group has >=3 flips).
decision_rule_written_before_run.no_support: otherwise: the exclusion has no measurable horizon association on this panel and no change to the policy is justified by these data.
decision_rule_written_before_run.either_way: the study reports the per-drop blind-threat rate and the checking-drop control, so a small absolute count is visible and cannot be read as a strength claim.

expected_evidence: results_qsearch_drop_exclusion.json (per-position records + aggregate + decision), plan-log.json with script/source hashes, README.md with scoped finding. Predicted outcome is genuinely open: blind-threat rate could be near zero (drops rarely create undefended attacks in these rules) or high.

cost_estimate.reason: expected single run well under the 120-minute threshold; no games, no training, no frozen-panel rerun

consumer: Decides whether the ordinary-drop exclusion in qsearch is a measurable even-depth evaluation blind spot in drop rules (and therefore whether even-depth comparisons like the hand-term d2 panel need a drop-aware caveat), or whether the policy is empirically harmless on generated drop rules.
explicit_nonclaims: not a strength or utility claim; no games are played
pseudo-attack geometry ignores pins, so 'undefended' is approximate
12 fixed rules, one position each: not a population statement about the generator
no change to product code, defaults, caps or frozen panels
done_condition: results file written with all 12 positions and the pre-written decision evaluated; README states the scoped answer and limits; hashes recorded; no claim beyond the measured set.
